name: Gold transmutation / supply technology
chain: A report claims that gold nuclei can be produced by nuclear transmutation.
First check reproducible yield, energy cost, usable output, isotope stability and commercial scale.
Only economically competitive, scalable production could materially change gold supply; a laboratory observation alone is insufficient.
A changed scarcity narrative could affect comparisons with Bitcoin, but adoption and capital flows would still need separate evidence.
gold: Potential supply pressure only if competitive production at meaningful scale is demonstrated; otherwise no established supply effect.
bitcoin: Ambiguous: a digital-scarcity narrative could benefit, while shared risk sentiment or liquidity could dominate.
counter: Look for an independently replicated cost per usable gram, annual capacity and actual changes in gold supply or ETF flows.
horizon: Years for a credible industrial supply change; narrative reactions could be faster.

name: Interest rates / central banks
pattern: \b(fed|federal reserve|ecb|central bank|interest rate|rate cut|rate hike|monetary policy|boe|bank of england)\b
chain: A headline concerns a central bank, interest rates or monetary policy.
Check the actual decision, prior market expectations and the central bank's guidance.
Policy surprises can change real yields, the dollar, borrowing costs and available liquidity.
Gold and Bitcoin may respond through different real-yield, liquidity and risk-appetite channels.
gold: Lower real yields can help a non-yielding asset; a stronger dollar or higher real yields can offset it.
bitcoin: Easier liquidity may help risk appetite, but recession concerns, leverage liquidations or regulation can offset it.
counter: Check inflation-adjusted yields, the dollar and the surprise relative to what markets already priced.
horizon: Hours to months, depending on the surprise and follow-through.

name: Inflation surprise
chain: A headline reports inflation or price pressure.
Compare the release with consensus and identify energy, core and demand components.
Higher inflation can increase demand for purchasing-power protection while also prompting tighter policy.
The balance between hedge demand and real-yield/liquidity effects determines the plausible asset channel.
gold: Inflation concern can support hedge demand; rising real yields or a stronger dollar can work against it.
bitcoin: Scarcity demand is possible, but tighter liquidity can hurt; a consistent inflation hedge is not established by the headline.
counter: Check core inflation, real yields, policy expectations and whether the surprise persists.

name: Banking / credit stress
pattern: \b(bank failure|bank run|banking crisis|credit stress|credit crunch|default|delinquenc|liquidity crisis|insolven|bankrupt)\b
chain: A headline flags potential credit, banking or repayment stress.
Distinguish an isolated borrower from system-wide funding pressure.
Forced deleveraging can initially create a demand for cash; later policy easing can change liquidity conditions.
Safe-haven demand and forced selling can therefore point in opposite directions.
gold: Safe-haven demand may support gold, while margin calls or a dollar shortage can initially force selling.
bitcoin: Risk reduction and leveraged selling may hurt first; later liquidity easing or distrust of intermediaries could support a different channel.
counter: Check credit spreads, funding markets, deposit data and the scale of policy support.
horizon: Immediate funding pressure through several quarters.

name: Sovereign debt / fiscal credibility
pattern: \b(sovereign|government debt|public debt|debt ceiling|budget deficit|fiscal|treasury auction|bond vigilante)\b
chain: A headline concerns public borrowing, fiscal policy or sovereign credit.
Check currency denomination, maturity, interest costs and the government's funding capacity.
A change in fiscal credibility can affect yields, currency confidence and expectations of future policy financing.
Debasement narratives and higher real yields can pull gold and Bitcoin in different directions.
gold: Currency-confidence concerns may help demand; higher real yields can be a headwind.
bitcoin: A scarcity narrative may attract attention, but capital controls, volatility and tighter funding can work against it.
counter: Check debt-service costs, auction results, currency moves and whether financing conditions actually deteriorate.

name: Bitcoin regulation / institutional flows
chain: A headline concerns digital assets, regulation or institutional participation.
Read the actual rule, filing or flow data; distinguish a proposal from an effective decision.
Changes to access, custody, funding or market integrity can alter Bitcoin demand and liquidity.
A gold effect requires evidence of substitution or a shared macro channel rather than an assumed one-for-one relationship.
gold: No automatic effect; look for actual substitution, gold ETF flows or shared dollar/real-yield changes.
bitcoin: Direction depends on access, enforceable rules, actual flows and whether the development was already priced.
counter: Check official filings, effective dates, net flows and leverage rather than social-media claims.
horizon: Days to months; implementation can take longer.

name: Energy / geopolitical supply shock
chain: A headline concerns a geopolitical or energy-supply shock.
Check whether physical supply or shipping is disrupted, and distinguish an announcement from delivery data.
Higher energy costs can lift inflation while weakening real spending and growth.
Safe-haven demand, policy responses and cash demand can create competing asset effects.
gold: Safe-haven demand can help, but real yields, the dollar and liquidation pressure still matter.
bitcoin: Often exposed to risk appetite and liquidity; a safe-haven response must be observed rather than assumed.
counter: Check physical energy supply, sustained price changes, real yields and cross-asset fund flows.

name: Gold demand / supply
chain: A headline concerns gold demand, production or market access.
Separate a price report from evidence of changed physical supply, official buying or investment flows.
A sustained change in demand or commercially usable supply can alter the gold balance.
Bitcoin would need a separate substitution, scarcity-narrative or shared-liquidity channel.
gold: Direction depends on whether net demand or economically usable supply changed and on the size relative to the market.
bitcoin: No direct mechanical link; substitution is a hypothesis that requires flow evidence.
counter: Check quantities, costs, central-bank disclosures, ETF flows and the size relative to annual gold supply.
horizon: Days to years, depending on physical capacity and demand persistence.

name: Growth / labour market
chain: A headline concerns growth or the labour market.
Compare the release with expectations, revisions and other activity measures.
Slower growth can weaken earnings and credit quality while changing expected interest rates.
Policy easing and risk aversion can compete, so one headline does not determine the asset direction.
gold: Lower real yields or defensive demand may help; cash demand and a stronger dollar can offset them.
bitcoin: Risk aversion can hurt; eventual easier liquidity could support a different outcome.
counter: Check revisions, unemployment, credit spreads and actual monetary conditions.
